  SOUTH GATE COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  8650 CALIFORNIA AVE

If you would like to participate in this meeting, you can participate via the following
options:

1. VIEW THE MEETING LIVE ONLINE AT: https://youtube.com/@SouthGateCA90280
Please allow up to 24 hours after the meeting for the archive to be available.
2. PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING by emailing the City Clerk at:
yglaze@sogate.org no later than 4:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please write
"Public Comment" in the subject line.
3. ATTEND THE MEETING IN PERSON
*The disruption in service of any alternative method does not prelude the City Council
or other legislative
body from taking further action and moving forward on the agenda.

Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,

  1
 closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 12pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be summarized
by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City Council and will
also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be recorded for
public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

Public Hearings - None
Comments From The Audience - Non-Agenda Items
During this time, members of the public may address the City Council regarding any items not
listed on the agenda and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council and not on
this agenda. Comments from the audience will be limited to three (3) minutes per speaker;
unless authorized by the Mayor, the time limit may not be extended by utilizing another
member's time. There will be no debate or action on items not listed on the agenda unless
authorized by law. The collective initial period of time for comments from the audience shall
be limited to 45 minutes. Any speaker that did not get a chance to speak during this segment
due to the 45-minute limitations will be able to speak at the end of the meeting prior to
adjournment.

Note: The City Council desires to provide all members of the public with the opportunity to
address the Council. Nevertheless, obscene language, comments intended to
disrupt/interfere, other actions which disrupt the progress of the meeting or slanderous
comments will not be tolerated and may result in ejection and/or may constitute a violation of
South Gate Municipal Code Section1.04.110.

Reports And Comments From City Officials
During this time, members of the City Council will report on matters pertaining to their service
on various intergovernmental boards and commissions as a representative of the City
pursuant to Assembly Bill 1234. City Council Members will also have an opportunity to
comment on matters not on the agenda.

Consent Calendar Items
Agenda Items 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 are Consent Calendar Items. All items including Ordinances,
Resolutions and Contracts, may be approved by adoption of the Consent Calendar,
individually and collectively by one (1) motion. There will be no separate discussion of these
items unless Members of the City Council, the public, or staff request that specific items be
removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion and action. Members of the
public are permitted to speak on any item listed but their time period is limited to three (3)
minutes in total.

Any motion to introduce or adopt an Ordinance on the Consent Calendar shall be: (1) a
motion to waive the reading of the Ordinance and introduce the Ordinance or (2) a motion to
waive the reading of the Ordinance and adopt the Ordinance, as appropriate.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

  6
 The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, email, mail. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such
times when a State of Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

SUBJECT:  AMENDMENT  N0.  1 TO  CONTRACT  N0.  2025-05-CC  WITH  NV5,  FOR

AND  LOCAL  ROADWAY  SAFETY  PLAN,  CITY  PROJECT  N0.  731-RPT

PURPOSE:  To approve  Amendment  No. 1 to Contract  No. 2025-05-CC  ("Amendment  No. 1")
with  NV5,  a California  corporation,  for additional  services  to prepare  the Comprehensive  Safety
Action  and Local  Roadway  Safety  Plan ("CSALRSP").

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  Ainendment  No. 1 to Contract  No. 2025-05-CC  with  NV5  ("Agreement")  for
  the preparation  of the Comprehensive  Safety  Action  and Local  Roadway  Safety  Plan City
  Project  No. 731-RPT,  for an amount  not-to-exceed  $1 7,460;

  Action  and Local  Roadway  Safety  Plan, City  Project  No. 731-RPT;  and

ANALYSIS:  As  part  of  Contract  No.  2025-05-CC,  NV5  is  contracted  to  prepare  the
Comprehensive  Safety  Action  and Local  Roadway  Safety  Plan  ("CSALRSP").  The  scope  of
work  was initially  based on the Department  of Transportation's  ("SS4A")  Grant  Self-Eligibility
List,  which  specifies  that  a CSALRSP  must  include  at least 7 out of 9 program  components.
However,  the  2024  SS4A  Grant  Notice  of  Funding  Opportunity  ("NOFO")  requires  all
components  listed  on the Self-Eligibility  List to be included  in the CSALRSP.

The Agreement  requires  the preparation  of seven of the nine components.  Amendment  No. 1 will
incorporate  the  remaining  two  program  elements  titled  "Policy  and  Process  Changes"  and
"Progress  and Transparency."

BACKGROUND:  Tlie City  of South  Gate's  ("City")  roadway  network  serves a variety  of users,
including  drivers,  pedestrians,  cydists,  and transit  riders.  With  aging  infrastructure,  high-traffic

  1

  12
 areas, and a dense population,  safety  is a key concern.  The CSALRSP  identifies  vulnerabilities,
particularly  in  high-crash  areas,  and  prioritizes  education  and other  safety  improvements  to
improve  roadway  conditions.  This  approacli  is important  for securing  federal  grant  funding  to
address these challenges.  The CSALRSP  is necessary  for both the Highway  Safety  Improvement
Program  ("HSIP")  and the SS4A  grant,  which  support  projects  aimed  at reducing  traffic  fatalities
and injuries.

All  nine components  outlined  in the SS4A  Grant  Self-Eligibility  List  and the NOFO  are required
to be included  in the CSALRSP  for a complete  approach  to roadway  safety.  These  components
are: Public  Coi'ni'nitment/Goal  Setting,  Safety  Data Analysis,  Planning  Structure,  Equity  Impact
Assessment,  Public  and Stakeliolder  Outreacli,  Policy  and Process  Changes,  Strategy  and Project
Selection,  Progress  and Transparency,  and Action  Plan Date.  Each covers  important  areas sucli
as data analysis,  safety  evaluation,  stakeholder  engagement,  and strategies  to improve  safety.
Including  all components  ensures the plan addresses  both irninediate  and long-teri'n  safety  needs,
fosters  collaboration  among  agencies,  organizations,  and the public,  and meets  funding  criteria
for a safer transportation  system.

NV5, Inc. (NV5) is excited  to have the opportunity  to provide  Professional  Engineering  Services  to the
City of South  Gate (City) for its Comprehensive  Safety Action  and Local Roadway  Safety  Plan
(CSALRSP). Our team  is quite familiar  with the Federal Safe Streets  For All (5544)  and has modeled
this proposal  on both the Self-Certification  Eligibility  Worksheet  and the City's RFTP. The RFTP is the
defining  smpe  of work; where the two documents  differ,  it is assumed  that the City will complete  the
tasks  identified  in the worksheet.

The 5544  worksheet  contains  the following  elements  required  for self-certifying  the City for
Implementation:  the items  in red (3, 7, and 9) are mandatory,  plus four out of the remaining  six
elements.  The items  in blue (1, 2, 4, and 5) are the ones that will be addressed  in this project.
  1.  Leadership  Commitment  (i.e. City Council  endorsement)
  2.  Planning  Strudure  (Advisory  Committee)
  3.  Safety Analysis
  4.  Engagement  and Collaboration  (stakeholders  and general  public)
  5.  Equity Considerations
  6.  Policy and Process  Changes
  7.  Strategy  and Project Selections
  8.  Progress  and Transparency
  9.  Adion  Plan Date (i.e., since 2019)

NV5 is a leader  in preparing  safety  action  plans and is experienced  and knowledgeable  in the Vision
Zero policy and the SS4A program.  Attached  to this proposal  are a few project  examples  that show
we are uniquely  qualified  to assist the City in this effort.  Our proposed  scope of work is as follows:

SCOPE OF WORK
The following  scope of work describes  and illustrates  in detail the methods  and processes  proposed
by NV5 to accomplish  the objectives  of the project.  The scope  is broken  down  into the tasks as
follows:

Task 1. Projed  Management,  Meetings,  and Coordination
At the start of the project,  NV5 will have an in-person  kick-off  meeting  with City staff  and the project
team to review the project  objectives,  schedule,  scope and approach.  We will meet with City staff and
other  invitees  eveiy two weeks,  alternating  between  in-person  and virtual  meetings  until the end of
the project  except  when other in-person  meetings  are already  scheduled.  A total of three  (3) in-
person  and three  (3) virtual  bi-weekly  meetings  are included  and shown  in the schedule.  In
preparation  of each meeting,  we will distribute  meeting  minutes  from the prior meeting  as well as an

It is expected  that the City will establish  an Advisory  Committee  called "The Safety Action  Plan Task
Force",  a multi-disciplinary  stakeholder  group,  representing  the Engineering  Department,  Traffic
Engineering,  police department,  fire districts,  advocacy  organizations,  disability  groups,  and possibly
senior  citizen  organizations.  The NV5 team will organize  and lead up to two (2) 90-minute  meetings
with the Task Force. Meetings  will address  one or more of the following  topics:  Plan Kick-Off  and
Overview,  Community  Outreach,  Goals and Objectives,  Crash Analysis  Findings,  High Injury Network,
and Policy Review and Recommendation.

Deliverables
  *  Agenda

  *  Action  Item Matrix
  *  Schedule  updates

Task 2. Review of Prior Plans
NV5 will review the City's prior Safety Action  Plan and use it as a starting  point for additional  analysis.
Because  the final CSALRSP will not include  policy recommendations  at this time,  no additional  work
will be completed  for this task.

Task3.  Crash HistoryAssessment&SafetyAnalysis
We will collect  data for the most recent five-years  available.  We will use the City's collision  database,
the Traffic  Information  Management  System  (TIMS), and the Statewide  Integrated  Traffic  Records
System  (SWITRS).

Based on the data collected,  NV5 will develop  an understanding  of where  crashes  are occurring  in
the City. Particular  focus  will be given to the fatal and injuiy crashes  to develop  a high-injury  network
(HIN). The final types of crashes  analyzed  will be determined  as directed  by the City and the Vision
Zero Task Force. Based on the NV5 team's  collective  experience  with developing  HINs for similar
Vision Zero Action  Plans, it is recommended  that the HIN for the City be developed  by also factoring
in moderate  injuiy crash locations  in addition  to fatal  and severe  injury crash  locations.  This
methodology  assists  in the development  of a more robust  HIN and factors  in crashes  that could  have
resulted  in severe  injury or fatalities,  especially  in the case of vulnerable  users such as pedestrians
and bicyclists.  We will develop  crash "heat  maps"  to identify  concentrations  of crash occurrences
and/or severity to visually identify areas of need or "hotspots" for further evaluation.

We will identify  both specific  and system-wide  needs, as revealed  by the crash analysis.  The hope is
that the contributing  factors  can inform  mitigation  measures  to reduce  overall  crash rates.

Deliverables
  *  Draft and Final Crash History Assessment  Memos
  *  Baseline  Safety Analysis  Report
  *  Spreadsheetofcrashdata(electronicfilesin.xlsxand.pdfformats)

Task 4. Countermeasure  Development
We will engage the stakeholders  in a single  public forum  to solicit  comments  on the analysis  and
present  a 'straw-man'  plan for countermeasures.

Physical  improvements  for up to 20 locations  will be identified  with the timeframe  for
implementation, high-level construction cost estimates, the lead agency/department, and other
relevant  details.  The final number  will depend  on the logical  breakdown  of HINs and advice from the
Advisoiy  Committee  and stakeholders.  The proposed  location  or corridor  will be displayed  in a
tabular  format,  along with a summary  of the details  for each recommended  intervention.

Proposed  capital  improvements  may include:  upgraded  or new traffic  signal equipment,
modifications  to signal  phasing, enhanced  crosswalks,  ADA upgrades,  traffic  calming  measures,  new
sidewalk and bike lanes, intersection or roadway @eometrymodifications, curb extensions, road
diets, new pavement markings, @uiderail, speed feedback devices, signage, and
reflectors/delineators, among other potential elements.

Programmatic  improvements  will not be included  in this CSALRSP; however,  if we find systemic
problems  as part of our analysis,  we will identify  them  in a separate  summary  document.  For
example,  if it is determined  that the crosswalk  standards  should  be changed,  those  would  be
included  in such a memo.

Deliverables
  *  Draff and Final Countermeasure  Development  Memos
  *  Summary  Memo  o( Stakeholder  and Public Engagement

Task 5. Implementation  Program
Following  the crash analysis,  the findings  will be applied  to develop  policy and project
recommendations  and ultimately,  the draft Vision Zero Safety Action  Plan. NV5 will engage  the
stakeholder  group again to both present  the findings  from Taks 4 and to solicit their  input on the
best practices  for Vision Zero Action  Plans, Complete  Street  practices,  and Safe System  standards
that are applicable  to the City. This will include  and consider  both local and national  best practices  in
safety  planning,  policy, and implementation.  We will identify  potential  funding  sources  for the
implementation  program.  These  best practices  will provide  relevant  examples  for proposed
infrastructure  improvements.

Deliverables
  *  Implementation  Program  Memo

Task 6. CSALRSP Development
A final  meeting  with the stakeholders  will precede  the development  of the draff CSALRSP (Safety
Action  Plan). The plan will tie together  each of the previous  tasks  in a concise  format  that makes  the
case for Vision Zero in the City and charts  a roadmap  for implementation.  We will disseminate  the
draft  plan to the stakeholders  for review and comment  and respond  to those  comments  as
appropriate.  We will aid the City in completing  the SS4A Self-Certification  Eligibility  Worksheet.

RHNA  Progress

The City's  RHNA  is summarized  in Table  #1 below  by income  level.  Income  levels  are set by the
HCD.  Each year HCD  publishes  annual  tables  of official  federal  and State income  limits.  HCD's
limits  are based on surveys  of local area median  income  ("AMI").  The most current  survey  is based
on information  release  May  9, 2024,  which  set the AMI  in Los Angeles  County  at $68,750  for a
single-person  household.  It is adjusted  by the number  ofpersons  per household.  Beginning  in 2022,
California  established  acutely  low-income  household  levels.  After  calculating  AMI  levels,  HCD
sets the maximum  acutely  low-income  limit  to equal 15 percent  of the county's  AMI,  adjusted  for
family  size. The income  categories  for a single-person  household  are as follows:

 Acutely  Low  15% or below  of AMI  Below  $10,350
 Extremely  low income  15% to 30% of AMI  Below  $29,150
 Very  low income  30% to 50% of AMI  Below  $48,550
 Low  income  50% to 80% of AMI  Below  $77,700
 Moderate  income  80% to 120%  of AMI  Below  $82,500

In Los Angeles  County,  as well  as several  other  counties  in the state, the very  low-income  limit

  2

 does not equal  50% of AMI  (and the low-income  limit  does not equal  80% of AMI).  There  are
many exceptions  to the arithmetic  calculation  of income  limits.  These include  adjustments  for high
housing  cost relative  to income,  the application  of state nonrnetropolitan  income  limits  in low-
income  areas, and national  maximums  in high-income  areas. In Los Angeles  County,  as well  as
several  others,  the magnitude  of these adjustments  results  in the low-income  limit  exceeding  AMI.

  INTRODUCTION

Government  Code  section  65400  requires  that each city, county,  or city and county,
including  charter  cities,  prepare  an annual  progress  report  (APR)  on the status  of the
housing  element  of its general  plan and progress  in its implementation,  using forms  and
definitions  adopted  by the California  Department  of Housing  and Community
Development  (HCD).  The following  form is to be used for satisfying  the reporting
requirements  of Government  Code section  65400,  subdivision  (a)(2).

These  forms  and instructions,  originally  adopted  March  27, 2010,  have been updated  to
incorporate  new housing  element  APR  requirements  pursuant  to legislation  including
Chapter  374, Statutes  of 2017  (Assembly  Bill 879); Chapter  366, Statutes  of 2017
(Senate  Bill 35); Chapter  659 Statutes  of 2022  (SB 6); and Chapter  647, Statutes  of
2022 (AB 2011 ), and Chapter  778, Statutes  of 2023  (Senate  Bill 423)

One primary  function  of housing  element  APR data is for HCD to track each local
government's  progress  towards  meeting  its annual  Regional  Housing  Needs  Allocation
(RHNA)  over the 5 or 8-year  planning  cycle. The key benchmark  for tracking  RHNA
progress  is issued  building  permits  reported  in Table A2.

How to submit  the Housinq  Element  Annual  Progress  Report  (APR)

The APR must be submitted  to HCD and the Governor's  Office  of Planning  and
Research  (OPR)  on or before  April 1 of each year using the forms  and tables  specified
by HCD. The APR  provides  information  for the previous  calendar  year and must be
submitted  separately  to both HCD and OPR (Gov. Code,  § 65400.).  There  are two
methods  available  for submitting  APRs:

  1.  New Online  Annual  Proqress  Reportinq  System  (HCD  Connect)  - This allows
  jurisdictions  to upload  directly  into HCD's  new database,  HCD Connect.  HCD
  Connect  is an online  portal  that will provide  the best user experience  by allowing
  jurisdictions  to submit  Housing  Elements,  Sites  Inventories  and APRs  on one
  platform.  To use the online  system,  you must register  with the link above  to
  create  a new account.  For jurisdiction  staff, you may need to create  a primary
  user account  or coordinate  with your existing  primary  user to register.  For
  consultants,  registering  will require  coordinating  with a representative  from the
  appropriate  jurisdiction.  If you are experiencing  issues  creating  or fogging  into
  your jurisdiction's account, please email HCDConnectHPD@hcd.ca.qov  or
  review HCD Connect User Portal Guide.

  "Above  moderate  income"  means  households  earning  more than 120 percent  of

  "Application  submitted"  means  an application  submittal  that has been determined

  "Area  Median  Income  (AMI)"  means  the median  household  income  based  on

  "Certificate  of occupancy  date"  is the date(s)  the certiTicate(s)  of occupancy,  or

  enforceable  agreement  within  a specific  timeframe  spanning  From the beginning
  of the RHNA  projection  and may be executed  throughout  the planning  period.
  Committed  Assistance  includes  obligating  funds  or other  in-kind  services  for
  affordable  units available  for occupancy  within  two years  of the agreement.

  "Completed  Entitlement"  means  a housing  development  or project  which  has
  received  all the required  land use approvals  or entitlements  necessaiy  for the
  issuance  of a building  permit.  This means  that there  is no additional  action

SUBJECT:  PURCHASE  ORDER AND APPROPRIATION  TO  FUND  REPAIRS  TO
THE ROADWAY  MEDIAN  ON FIRESTONE BOULEVARD

PURPOSE:  To approve a purchase order with Carol Electric Company, Inc., a California
corporation, and funding appropriation to fully fund repairs to. the Firestone Boulevard median
located between Santa Fe Avenue and Calden Avenue.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council will consider:
  a.  Authorizing the City Manager to approve a Purchase Order with Carol Electric Company,
  Inc., on a sole-source basis for repairs to the electrical and irrigation systems of the
  Firestone Boulevard Median, located between Santa Fe Avenue and Calden Avenue, in an
  amount not to exceed $165,700; and
  b.  Appropriating  $190,000 in Gas Tax Funds to fund the repairs and construction
  contingency.

FISCAL IMPACT:  There is no impact to the General Fund. The $165,700 Purchase Order is
proposed to be funded through the recorninended Gas Tax Funds appropriation of $190,000, which
includes $14,300 in contingency funds.

ANALYSIS:  The raised landscape median on Firestone Boulevard located between Santa Fe
Avenue and Alameda Street was vandalized. The electrical and irrigation systems were damaged
and are now inoperable. The Public Works Department's policy is to complete repairs on an urgent
basis to protect public health and safety, as well as to ensure the timely completion of repairs to
city infrastructure. Public Works recommends awarding a purchase order to Carol Electric, Inc.,
as a sole-source contractor for the necessary electrical repairs.

Carol Electric, Inc., has previously worked on the Firestone Boulevard median, having been a sub-
contractor during a prior project that included the installation of up-light fixtures and landscape
enhancements. Its familiarity  with the project, coupled with its experience  in electrical  work
related to the median's lighting system, makes Carol Electric, Inc., the ideal candidate to efficiently
carry  out the required  repairs.

  I

  119
 In accordance with South Gate Municipal Code § 1.54.510, the electrical work by Carol Electric,
Inc., to restore tlie lighting system will be conducted on an accelerated schedule, prioritizing safety.
This action is necessary to address iini'nediate safety concerns arising from the lack of functional
lighting. The emergency designation will allow the work to proceed without delay, ensuring that
the lighting system is restored as quickly as possible. Contracting with Carol Electric, Inc., will
expedite the repair process due to their knowledge of the existing systems and their established
history of working on similar projects. By engaging  a contractor already familiar with the work,
Public Works can ensure tliat the necessary repairs are completed swiftly, effectively, and within
budget.

BACKGROUND:  Firestone Boulevard features raised landscape medians, an irrigation system,
and an electrical system, including up-light fixtures that enhance visibility  at night, reduce
accidents, and help manage traffic flow, contributing to overall safety. The irrigation system also
supports the health of the median's landscaping, improving  the aesthetic value of the corridor.

Recently, the electrical wiring powering both the irrigation and up-lighting systems on Firestone
Boulevard was stolen. In addition, the up-light fixtures, electrical conduits, and irrigation boxes
were severely vandalized, leaving the median without electricity and disabling both the lighting
and irrigation  systems.

If left unaddressed, this situation could result in several negative outcomes, including:

  Reduced  Safety: The lack of operational up-light fixtures will significantly  diminish
  visibility  for drivers, especially at night, increasing  safety hazards along  Firestone
  Boulevard.

  *  Damage to Landscaping: Without a functioning irrigation system, the trees, shrubs, and
  plants in the median are at risk of deteriorating or dying, causing a loss of valuable
  landscaping that enhances the area's visual appeal.

  *  Increased Maintenance Costs: If the situation is not addressed promptly,  further damage
  may occur, leading to higher repair and replacement costs.

Carol Electric, Inc., will work to address the repair of the electrical and irrigation systems to be
repaired simultaneously, thereby minimizing the downtime of the median's systems and ensuring
that safety and aesthetics are restored as quickly as possible.

Additionally,  to prevent future theft and vandalism of the wiring and fixtures, Carol Electric, Inc.,
will implement enhanced security measures. These measures include adding a concrete slurg mix
to the electrical concrete pull boxes and locking the lids, making it more difficult for thieves to
access and steal the wiring. These proactive steps are designed to mitigate the risk of future theft
and vandalism, helping to protect the City's investment in the Firestone Boulevard median.

ANALYSIS:  Construction  of the Project  is complete.  Staff  are preparing  to release  the final
payment  to Sequel  Contractors,  Inc. The Public  Contract  Code  Section  7107  establishes  that the
City  must  accept  the  completion  of  construction  and  issue  a public  notice  of  such  prior  to
releasing  the final  payment  on construction  projects.  The Notice  of Completion  ("NOC")  meets

  1  124
 this requirement.  It provides  written  notice  to concerned  parties  that all work  on the project  has
been  completed.  The  NOC  initiates  the  35-day  period  within  which  concerned  parties  may
exercise  their  lien rights  for the work  they performed  on the Project.  The City  may use a part, or
all,  of the 5% retention  payment  to settle  any  liens  exercised  against  the City.  If no liens  or

claims  have been filed  within  35 days of the filing  of the NOC,  the City  will  release the retention
and any remaining  amounts  due to the Contractor.

Contract  No.  2023-14-CC  required  a 5% retention  be held from  construction  invoice  payments,
which  totaled  $228,849  and released  within  60 days of completion  of the work.  Construction  was
completed  on September  13, 2024;  thus, the retention  payment  is due.

BACKGROUND:  The  Project  is budgeted  in the Fiscal  Year  2024/25  Capital  Improvement
Program  (FY  2024/25  CIP).  The improvements  constructed  include  bicycle  lanes on (1) Garfield
Avenue  from  Firestone  Boulevard  to Harding  Avenue,  (2) Gardendale  Street  between  Garfield
Avenue  and the Los Angeles  River,  and (3) Frontage  Road from  Southern  Avenue  to Miller  Way
and back  to end of west  Frontage  Road.  The  Project  improvements  constructed  include  bike
lanes and amenities,  sharrows,  raised  laridscape  medians  with  drought  tolerant  plants  and trees,
ADA  improvements,  sidewalk  repairs,  signing  and  striping,  storm  water  mitigation
improvements,  new crosswalks  with  flashing  beacons,  and new curbs and gutters.

On  February  28,  2023,  the  City  Council  approved  Contract  No.  2023-14-CC  with  Sequel
Contractors,  Inc., for the construction  of Garfield  Avenue  Complete  Street,  City  Project  No. 564-
ST,  in an amount  not-to-exceed  $5,052,943.  Construction  began  on May  15,  2023,  and was
completed  on September  13, 2024.  Required  documentation  was  completed  on February  28,
2025.

Two  change  orders  were approved  as part of this project,  as follows:

  *  On  February  28,  2023,  upon  awarding  the  contract,  the  City  Council  approved  a
  deductive  Change  Order  (CCO  No.  1)  for  $548,600.  This  modification  reduced  the
  amount  of concrete  in the median  islands,  replacing  it with  landscaping,  and adjusted  the
  original  contract  amount  to $4,504,343.

  @  Change  Order  No.  2,  in  the  amount  of  $231,193,  was  required  to  complete  the
  construction  of bioswales,  install  solar  controllers  in the City  of Downey,  and address
  additional  items requested  by the City.

The final  construction  cost was $4,576,975.

The contractor  has fulfilled  all contract  obligations,  completing  the work  in accordance  with
approved  plans and specifications  while  maintaining  quality  craftsmanship,  staying  within
budget,  and meeting  the project  timeline.  The project  completed  has been inspected  and
confirmed  to meet all required  standards.

The City  Council  is now positioned  to accept the completion  of the Project  and file the Notice  of
Completion  with  the Los Angeles  County  Registrar  Recorder's  Office.
